about.description:
mathparse parses and evaluates mathematical expressions written in
natural language. It handles arithmetic, unary and binary operators and
word-based numbers across a number of languages, returning the computed
result from a plain string such as "four plus four".
about.summary: mathparse is a library for solving mathematical equations contained in strings

name: mathparse
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  version: "0.2.9"

package:
  name: mathparse
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/m/mathparse/mathparse-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 39076aaedce5219942df6204f67548f4a05529f7c478c0d1a65b50e16694712c

build:
  number: 0
  noarch: python
  script: ${{ PYTHON }} -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation

requirements:
  host:
    - python ${{ python_min }}.*
    - pip
    - setuptools
  run:
    - python >=${{ python_min }},<3.15

tests:
  - python:
      imports:
        - mathparse
      pip_check: true
      python_version:
        - ${{ python_min }}.*
        - "*"
  - script:
      - python -c "from mathparse import mathparse; assert mathparse.parse('four plus four', language='ENG') == 8"

about:
  homepage: https://github.com/gunthercox/mathparse
  repository: https://github.com/gunthercox/mathparse
  documentation: https://mathparse.chatterbot.us
  license: MIT
  license_file: LICENSE
  summary: mathparse is a library for solving mathematical equations contained in strings
  description: |
    mathparse parses and evaluates mathematical expressions written in
    natural language. It handles arithmetic, unary and binary operators and
    word-based numbers across a number of languages, returning the computed
    result from a plain string such as "four plus four".

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - killua156
